scenario: IKEA ML 面试，你想说你把前端从两次 API 调用优化成一次、省了约一秒；上次你说成「I decoupled the API, one call rather than two」，绕且用词不准。
scenario_en: In an IKEA ML interview you want to say you cut the front end from two API calls down to one, saving about a second; last time it came out as "I decoupled the API, one call rather than two."
q: 「合并调用、省一次往返」这个优化，该怎么一句说清？
q_en: How do you say the "merge the calls, save a round trip" optimization in one clean line?
options: I decoupled the API, so on the front end we only need one call rather than the previous two, so it saves about one second.
We collapse the two calls into a single round trip, so the page loads with one request instead of two.
So we call the API twice — once when the page loads, then the user changes a bit, then we call it again...
The quantity of API invocations was reduced from two to one, thereby decreasing aggregate page latency.
options_en: I decoupled the API, so on the front end we only need one call rather than the previous two, so it saves about one second.
We collapse the two calls into a single round trip, so the page loads with one request instead of two.
So we call the API twice — once when the page loads, then the user changes a bit, then we call it again...
The quantity of API invocations was reduced from two to one, thereby decreasing aggregate page latency.
tradeoff: 地道「one round trip」vs 卡壳直译：round trip 一词点出省的是网络往返；「decouple / one call rather than two」绕半天没说到机制。
why: 用「collapse the two calls into one round trip」点名机制——省的是一次网络往返，不是「decouple API」；动词落到 round trip 或 request 上。
why_en: Say we collapse the two calls into one round trip — the win is cutting a network round trip, not decoupling the API.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官只想听结论、不深究机制，直接说「we cut it to one request」也够，不必展开 round trip。
optionMeanings: 「decoupled，一次不是两次」，绕着说省一秒。
「合并成一次 round trip」，点出省的是往返。
反复数调用次数，绕「先一次、再一次」。
书面被动语态，陈述调用从二减到一。
optionMeanings_en: "Decoupled the API, one call not two" — talks around a one-second saving.
"Collapse into one round trip" — names the saved network trip.
Keeps counting call counts, looping "once, then again."
Passive written register stating invocations dropped two to one.
optionScenarioImpacts: decouple 用错，面试官听不出你省的是往返。
机制清楚，面试官立刻抓到优化点。
一直在数次数，始终没说出优化本身。
像念论文，口语场合显生硬。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: "Decouple" is wrong; they can't tell you saved a trip.
Mechanism is clear; they catch the win instantly.
You keep counting; the optimization never lands.
Reads like a paper — stiff when said out loud.
optionDirectness: 错在动词——decouple 不是这里的机制。
抓住 round trip：省的是一次网络往返。
错在打转，只复述调用没给结论。
错在语域，被动书面腔不像对话。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong verb — decouple isn't the mechanism here.
Nails round trip: the win is one fewer network trip.
Wrong because it loops on calls, gives no conclusion.
Wrong register — passive written style isn't conversation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端发一个请求到服务端再拿回响应的一次网络往返；合并调用就是减少往返次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A round trip is one request from client to server and back; collapsing calls cuts the number of round trips.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统之间约定好的调用接口，前端按它请求后端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the agreed interface one system calls another through.

scenario: 系统设计面试问实时更新怎么做。你想表达「服务端主动推、客户端不用反复轮询」，但容易说成「前端一直问后端有没有新数据」。
scenario_en: A system-design interview asks how you'd do real-time updates. You want to say "the server pushes, the client doesn't keep polling," but it tends to come out as "the front end keeps asking the back end."
q: 「服务端推送、不用轮询」这个机制，该怎么地道说出口？
q_en: How do you say the "server pushes, no polling" mechanism naturally?
options: The server pushes updates over a WebSocket, so the client doesn't have to poll.
The front end keeps asking the back end again and again if there's any new data.
So the front end, it keeps calling, calling the server to check for updates...
A persistent bidirectional connection is established to facilitate real-time message propagation.
options_en: The server pushes updates over a WebSocket, so the client doesn't have to poll.
The front end keeps asking the back end again and again if there's any new data.
So the front end, it keeps calling, calling the server to check for updates...
A persistent bidirectional connection is established to facilitate real-time message propagation.
tradeoff: 地道「push … doesn't have to poll」vs 直译「keeps asking again and again」：push/poll 一组词点出机制，「一直问」听着像不懂推送。
why: 用「push over a WebSocket … so the client doesn't have to poll」把机制框成推 vs 轮询；关键词是 push / poll，不是「一遍遍问」。
why_en: Frame it as push versus poll — the server pushes over a WebSocket so the client doesn't have to keep polling.
whenOtherWins: 更新不频繁、场景简单时，long-polling 或定时轮询就够，不必上 WebSocket。
optionMeanings: 点名推 vs 轮询：服务端主动推、客户端不问。
「前端一遍遍问后端有没有新数据」，把推送说成反复轮询。
卡在「keeps calling, calling」原地打转。
书面定义句，陈述「持久双向连接」。
optionMeanings_en: "Server pushes over a WebSocket, client doesn't poll" — names push vs poll.
"Front end keeps asking" — describes push as repeated polling.
Stuck on "keeps calling, calling," spinning in place.
A textbook line stating "a persistent bidirectional connection."
optionScenarioImpacts: push/poll 一组词，面试官立刻懂机制。
听着像不懂推送、只会轮询。
循环卡壳，没给出任何机制词。
像背定义，不像在解释设计。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The push/poll pairing lands the mechanism at once.
Sounds like you only know polling, not push.
Looping stall — no mechanism word ever surfaces.
Reads as a memorized definition, not an explanation.
optionDirectness: 抓住 push vs poll：服务端推、客户端不轮询。
错在方向——把推送描述成轮询。
错在打转，动词重复没落点。
错在语域，定义腔口语里僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Nails push vs poll: server pushes, client doesn't poll.
Wrong direction — describes push as polling.
Wrong because it loops; repeated verb, no landing.
Wrong register — definition style is stiff out loud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条持久的双向连接，服务端可主动向客户端推送消息，不用客户端反复请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent two-way connection where the server can push messages to the client without repeated requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端按固定间隔反复请求服务端，问有没有新数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polling is the client repeatedly asking the server whether there's new data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端发请求后服务端挂住连接、有更新才回，是轮询的省事变体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Long-polling holds the request open until the server has an update, a lighter variant of polling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端通过一条长连接单向持续向客户端推事件，比 WebSocket 轻但只能单向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server-Sent Events (SSE) is a one-way stream where the server pushes events to the client over one long-lived connection.

scenario: Alterion 技术面聊 REST vs GraphQL，你想说「要保证前后端的请求/响应结构对齐」；上次你说成「validate the passing parameters if the structure is cracked with back end」，词不准。
scenario_en: In an Alterion tech interview on REST vs GraphQL you want to say "keep the front-end and back-end request/response shapes aligned," but last time it came out as "validate the passing parameters if the structure is cracked with back end."
q: 「锁定前后端接口结构、别让它漂移」该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "pin down the interface shape so it doesn't drift"?
options: We validate the passing parameters in case the structure is cracked with the back end.
So we align the format, the request format and the response format, make sure they're the same...
We pin down the API contract up front so the request and response schema don't drift.
The interface specification must be mutually agreed upon to guarantee structural consistency.
options_en: We validate the passing parameters in case the structure is cracked with the back end.
So we align the format, the request format and the response format, make sure they're the same...
We pin down the API contract up front so the request and response schema don't drift.
The interface specification must be mutually agreed upon to guarantee structural consistency.
tradeoff: 地道「API contract / schema drift」vs 卡壳「structure is cracked」：contract、schema 是行话，「cracked」听着不知在说什么。
why: 用「API contract」+「schema don't drift」表达前后端对齐；「structure is cracked」不是这个概念的行话。
why_en: Call it the API contract and say the request and response schema shouldn't drift — "the structure is cracked" isn't how we say it.
whenOtherWins: 若只想说「前后端先对齐格式」，一句「we agree on the request and response format first」也够，不必上 contract 一词。
optionMeanings: 想说结构对齐，却用错了词。
反复念 format 一样，绕不出。
锁定接口约定，说清结构不漂移。
书面「须双方约定」定义腔。
optionMeanings_en: "Validate parameters, in case structure is cracked" — wrong words for alignment.
Loops on "request format, response format, the same," never lands.
"Pin down the API contract, schema doesn't drift" — names the mechanism.
Textbook "interface specification must be agreed" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 行话到位，面试官立刻懂。
像念规范文档，不像对话。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: "Structure is cracked" leaves them unsure what you mean.
You keep restating "format," with no real term.
Contract / schema are the words; they get it at once.
Reads like reciting a spec, not a conversation.
optionDirectness: 错在打转，重复 format 没落点。
抓住接口约定：结构不漂移。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong word — "cracked" isn't how this concept is said.
Wrong because it loops on format, never reaches contract.
Nails API contract: the schema doesn't drift.
Wrong register — spec-speak is stiff out loud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前后端约定好的请求/响应结构与语义，双方都照它实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API contract is the agreed request/response shape and semantics both sides implement against.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前后端的数据结构随时间不一致、对不上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Schema drift is when the front-end and back-end data shapes fall out of sync over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源 URL 操作的一种接口风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that operates on resource URLs using HTTP verbs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种查询语言，前端按需声明要哪些字段，一次取回、少 over-fetch。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language where the client declares exactly which fields it wants in one request.

scenario: 系统设计面试问「返回列表怎么翻页」。你想说「用 cursor 翻页，避免插入新数据时页面错位」，但容易只说「按页码一页页给」。
scenario_en: A system-design interview asks how you'd paginate a list. You want to say "page with a cursor so inserts don't shift the page," but it tends to shrink to "give pages by number."
q: 「用 cursor 分页、避免错位」该怎么地道说出口？
q_en: How do you say "cursor-based pagination, no shifting" naturally?
options: So we cut the data into pages by number and give the front end one page at a time...
The result set is partitioned into discrete pages via a positional offset parameter.
We use offset paging — skip the first N, take the next N — even though new rows shift the page.
We use cursor-based pagination, so new rows don't shift the results as you page.
options_en: So we cut the data into pages by number and give the front end one page at a time...
The result set is partitioned into discrete pages via a positional offset parameter.
We use offset paging — skip the first N, take the next N — even though new rows shift the page.
We use cursor-based pagination, so new rows don't shift the results as you page.
tradeoff: 地道「cursor-based pagination … don't shift」vs 直译「一页页给」：cursor 一词点出为什么不错位；「by number」没说到机制。
why: 用「cursor-based pagination」点名机制——游标锚在稳定排序键上，插入新行不会让页面错位；offset 会错位。
why_en: Say cursor-based pagination — the cursor anchors on a stable key, so inserts don't shift your page the way offset would.
whenOtherWins: 数据基本不变、翻页不深时，offset/limit 更简单——接口只传两个整数，够用。
optionMeanings: 「按页码切成一页页给前端」，绕着说没点机制。
书面「用 offset 参数把结果集切成离散页」。
「offset 分页，跳 N 取 N」，承认插入新行会错位。
点名游标分页，插入新行也不会让页错位。
optionMeanings_en: "Cut into pages by number, one at a time" — talks around it.
Textbook "partition the result set via an offset parameter."
"Offset paging, skip N take N" — admits inserts shift the page.
"Cursor-based pagination, inserts don't shift" — names the mechanism.
optionScenarioImpacts: 没说出为什么不错位，面试官听不到机制。
像念定义，且暴露的是会错位的 offset。
方案本身在深翻/频繁插入时会错位。
cursor 一词点出为什么页面不漂。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Never says why it won't shift; the mechanism is lost.
Sounds like a definition, and picks shift-prone offset.
The approach itself shifts on deep paging or inserts.
The word cursor shows exactly why the page holds.
optionDirectness: 错在打转，「一页页给」没说到机制。
错在语域，定义腔又选了会错位的方案。
错在场景——offset 在本题的插入下会错位。
抓住 cursor：锚在稳定键上，插入不错位。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong because it loops; "page by page" skips the mechanism.
Wrong register — definition style, and shift-prone offset.
Wrong for this case — offset shifts under the inserts here.
Nails cursor: anchored on a stable key, inserts don't shift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把长列表切成一页页返回，避免一次拉全量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pagination splits a long list into pages instead of returning everything at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页末条的稳定键(cursor)做下一页起点，插入新行不会让页错位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor-based pagination uses the last row's stable key as the next page's start, so inserts don't shift the page.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用「跳过前 N 条、取 N 条」翻页，简单但插入新行会让页错位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offset pagination skips N rows and takes N; simple, but inserting rows shifts the page.
